sources.researchNote: Entry for the pianist and teacher (Zhytomyr, 2 September 1888 – Warsaw, 10 June 1962): pupil of Aleksander Michałowski at the Warsaw Music Institute, 1905–13; professor of piano at the school of the Warsaw Music Society from 1918, from 1919 the Fryderyk Chopin Higher School of Music, a post he held until 1950; professor at the State Higher School of Music in Warsaw from 1951 and dean of its piano faculty 1953–59; juror of the first three International Chopin Competitions. The entry names Kaper among Śmidowicz’s pupils, beside Władysław Szpilman, Witold Lutosławski, Leon Boruński and Wacław Grzybowski. It is an independent witness to the teaching relation that the archive otherwise documents through the school concert of June 1925, and it establishes what was taught: piano, in Śmidowicz’s class at the Chopin school.
